boundary_rationale: The voice turns first-person plural and direct-address at 14:7: “Though our iniquities testify against us, work for your name’s sake, Yahweh” (web:Jer.14.7) spliced אִם עֲוֺנֵ֨ינוּ֙ עָ֣נוּ (oshb:Jer.14.7, byte tier) -- a scene shift from the third-person drought description just given to the people's own plea. The petition (our rebellions, our sins) and the appeal to Yahweh as “the hope of Israel” (14:8) run through the closing plea “don’t leave us” (14:9), a bounded communal cry.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row backward to include the drought description (14:1-6) was considered: both concern the same distress, but the shift from third-person report to first-person-plural direct address to Yahweh is a scene change strong enough to keep the plea as its own unit.
literature_type_guess: communal penitential plea invoking Yahweh's name
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A setumah closes this row at its own final verse, Jer.14.9; the mark rests on WLC alone, single-witness, at tier-3, weak corroborative standing in the Prophets. Jer.14.6, just ahead of this row's opening, is unmarked.

boundary_rationale: “Yahweh says to this people” (web:Jer.14.10) carries כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier): the lamed phrase addresses the pronouncement to the people, while its third-person forms, אָֽהֲבוּ֙, עֲוֺנָ֔ם and חַטֹּאתָֽם (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), mark the oracle’s subject rather than its addressee -- a distinct footing from both the address to the deity in the communal plea before it and the private address to Jeremiah that opens next at 14:11. This one verse closes its own thought: remembered iniquity, punished sin.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into the communal plea that precedes it, as the divine answer completing one exchange, was considered: the topic (the people's fate) carries over from 14:7-9, but the addressee shifts from Yahweh, addressed in the plea, to the people, addressed here by the lamed phrase, which this row keeps separate.
literature_type_guess: one-verse divine refusal oracle answering the people's plea
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Immediately before this row opens, Jer.14.9 carries a setumah; Jer.14.10, the row's own verse, carries a second setumah of its own. Both marks rest on WLC alone at tier-3, weak corroborative standing in the Prophets. The verse refers to the divine name in the third person, וַיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א רָצָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.14.10, byte tier), and carries no first-person clause; the first first-person divine clauses in this stretch stand at 14:12.

boundary_rationale: “Yahweh said to me” (web:Jer.14.11) opens וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּ֛ל (oshb:Jer.14.11, byte tier) -- a scene shift to private address to Jeremiah, instructing him not to intercede, distinct from 14:10’s pronouncement about the people at large. “Then I said” (web:Jer.14.13) is Jeremiah’s own protest within that same exchange, citing prophets who promise “assured peace”; “Then Yahweh said to me” (web:Jer.14.14) answers him on the same opening shape that carries the row’s own onset, וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Jer.14.14, byte tier; that shape, sweep: 13 verses book-wide), and the reply exposing the lying prophets runs through 14:14-16. The recurrence is not cut because it marks a turn within one sustained private exchange rather than a fresh commission -- the same shape carries the onset at 15:1, where a genuinely fresh reply begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row at 14:13 (Jeremiah's protest) or at 14:14 (Yahweh's extended reply) was considered: the addressee does alternate at each turn, the prophet addressing the deity at 14:13 and the deity answering him at 14:14, but both stay inside one sustained private exchange between the same two participants. That is unlike the seam four verses on, where the material closing at 14:22 is a communal plea addressed to the deity by a first-common-plural voice, a different speaker role and a different unit type, corroborated by the petuchah there (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration only) -- so the dialogue here was kept whole while the seam at 14:22 into 15:1 was not.
literature_type_guess: private dialogue oracle exposing the lying prophets

device_notes: A setumah break sits at Jer.14.10, immediately ahead of this span's own opening; the mark rests on WLC alone, single-witness, at tier-3, weak corroborative standing in the Prophets. Further setumah breaks recur inside the span at Jer.14.12, Jer.14.13, and Jer.14.14; Jer.14.14 also holds a doubled ketiv/qere site, consulted here but not spliced into this row. Two paseq segs fall inside the span as well, at Jer.14.13 and Jer.14.16; the paseq inventory itself is single-witness and count-only, so neither seg's position within its verse can be sourced from that layer.

boundary_rationale: “Have you utterly rejected Judah” (web:Jer.14.19) opens הֲמָאֹ֨ס מָאַ֜סְתָּ אֶת יְהוּדָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.14.19, byte tier) -- the voice returns to first-person-plural direct address to Yahweh, a scene shift from the commissioned dirge just closed back to the people's own petition. “We acknowledge, Yahweh, our wickedness” (14:20) and the appeal to the rain-giving Creator (14:22) carry the plea to its close, a bounded communal cry paired with the one at 14:7-9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row forward into 15:1 (Yahweh's reply) was considered: 15:1 does answer the plea just voiced, but it is addressed to Jeremiah rather than to Yahweh, a scene change kept as the start of a separate row.

boundary_rationale: “For who will have pity on you, Jerusalem?” (web:Jer.15.5) turns to second-feminine-singular direct address, כִּ֠י מִֽי יַחְמֹ֤ל עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.15.5, byte tier) -- Jerusalem addressed by name rather than by the third-person language of 15:1-4. The poem moves between that direct address (15:5-6) and third-person description of the widows and the destroyer (15:7-9) without a further scene change, closing on the neum-YHWH formula at 15:9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row where the grammar shifts from second-person address (15:5-6) to third-person description (15:7-9) was considered: Hebrew poetry moves between address and description within one sustained poem routinely, so no fresh row was opened there.
literature_type_guess: direct-address dirge over Jerusalem's bereaved widows

device_notes: This row's own close, Jer.15.9, carries a setumah; the mark is attested by WLC alone, single-witness, at tier-3, weak corroborative standing in the Prophets; the same verse carries one note in the separate single-witness ketiv/qere inventory, the unpointed ketiv באה beside the pointed qere בָּ֥א (oshb:Jer.15.9, byte tier). Jer.15.4, just before the opening, carries no parashah mark, though that verse carries its own note in the ketiv/qere inventory, the unpointed ketiv לזועה beside the pointed qere לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.4, byte tier).

boundary_rationale: “Woe is me, my mother” (web:Jer.15.10) opens אֽוֹי לִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֣י יְלִדְתִּ֗נִי (oshb:Jer.15.10, byte tier) -- another oy apostrophe (sweep: 8 verses book-wide, the same lexeme spliced at 13:27 above), here turned inward as Jeremiah's own outcry rather than a judgment against the city, a clean scene shift from the divine judgment speech just closed. A reply opens at 15:11 on a bare divine-name formula, אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier) -- neither a word-event shape nor a koh-amar -- and runs through 15:14; the prophet’s own voice resumes at 15:15, אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier), and the first-person complaint holds through 15:16-15:18. “Therefore Yahweh says” (web:Jer.15.19), on לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier), therefore opens a second divine reply with a changed speaking mouth -- a licensed seam this unit declines to cut, because the adversaries it answers are the same ones already named in the complaint rather than a newly entered participant. Complaint and both replies run together to the closing promise of deliverance at 15:21.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the row at 15:19 was considered, since לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) resumes the divine voice after the prophet’s own complaint runs from 15:15 through 15:18 and so does change the speaking mouth -- a licensed seam, not a non-event. It was set aside because no new participant enters there: the adversaries met with deliverance in 15:19-21 are the same ones already named in the complaint, כֻּלֹּ֥ה מְקַלְלַֽונִי (oshb:Jer.15.10, byte tier) at 15:10 and מֵרֹ֣דְפַ֔י (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier) at 15:15, so one participant set spans the exchange.
literature_type_guess: individual complaint-and-reply dialogue between Jeremiah and Yahweh

Jer.15.11 and Jer.15.16, both inside the span, each carry one further note in the separate single-witness ketiv/qere inventory: the unpointed ketiv שרותך beside the pointed qere שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), and the unpointed ketiv דבריך beside the pointed qere דְבָֽרְךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.15.16, byte tier).

boundary_rationale: “Then Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Jer.16.1), rendering vayehi debar-YHWH וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.16.1, byte tier) -- one of the book's narrative word-event onsets. The command that follows, “You shall not take a wife” (web:Jer.16.2), opens on לֹֽא תִקַּ֥ח לְךָ֖ אִשָּׁ֑ה (oshb:Jer.16.2, byte tier), its own koh-amar rationale running from 16:3 through 16:4. A second command in the same voice follows without a scene change: “Don't enter into the house of mourning” (web:Jer.16.5) carries its koh-amar formula in the same verse as the prohibition itself, כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל תָּבוֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית מַרְזֵ֔חַ (oshb:Jer.16.5, byte tier), with 16:6-7 running on as that command's rationale and carrying no formula of its own. A third command, “You shall not go into the house of feasting” (web:Jer.16.8), closes with the full divine-name stack “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says”, כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier). The three prohibitions stay one row because the second-person-singular addressee of the commands at 16:2, 16:5 and 16:8 never changes; the second-person-plural at לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם וּבִֽימֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier) sits inside the quoted oracle content, addressing the people the oracle describes rather than marking a fresh frame addressee, and each koh-amar onset explains the command just given rather than opening a new frame-owner.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 16:1-9 as a symbolic_act_report alongside the book's other enacted signs was considered and set aside: the span pairs its three prohibitions with their own rationale without narrating Jeremiah's own compliance in a first-person performance clause the way the potter's-house sign that opens the next frame does (web:Jer.18.3), so the material was kept in command-and-rationale form as judgment_oracle.
literature_type_guess: sign-oracle: paired command-and-rationale prohibitions barring marriage, mourning, and feasting
